question: What can the official LPPCHEA Ramsar Information Sheet and related public records establish about the reported 2001 ERDB fish survey, and do other documents independently validate its eight-fish count?

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the official Ramsar Information Sheet directly and cross-checked its fish paragraph against JICA's searchable reproduction. The RIS is the 2013 LPPCHEA Ramsar site information sheet; the direct PDF was also retained locally for visual review.
relevantSections: Ecological character / fish species paragraph reporting an ERDB survey in 2001 and day/night sampling.
RIS references, including Alba et al. (2009), not explicitly linked to the fish paragraph as its source.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed Appendix 17 through browser-extracted PDF text, including the LPPCHEA fish-species subsection and its source attribution.
relevantSections: Appendix 17, fish species subsection for LPPCHEA, PDF page 44 / appendix page App 17-7.
Source line explicitly cites the Information Sheet on Ramsar Wetlands (RIS): LPPCHEA, updated February 2013, Ramsar Convention Secretariat.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Downloaded the official six-page committee-report PDF and visually reviewed all rendered pages. Page 1 contains an aggregate eight-fish statement; the remaining pages discuss the proposed legislation and do not cite a fish source or list taxa.
relevantSections: Cover: Committee Report HLUUD 046 S-2023, PCR 323-2023, dated 5 June 2023.
Page 1: aggregate biodiversity paragraph reports eight fish species for LPPWP without taxa, method, date, or citation.
Pages 2-6: legislative analysis and recommendation; no fish bibliography or underlying survey citation found.
sourceAccess.documentNumberCaveat: The cover identifies PCR 323-2023 while the body footer appears to identify PCR 321-2023. This internal numbering discrepancy does not affect the limited aggregate statement reviewed.

reportedStudy.locationContextAsReported: Las Piñas-Parañaque Critical Habitat and Ecotourism Area (LPPCHEA), as named in the Ramsar Information Sheet.
reportedStudy.samplingContextAsReported: Four fish species were reported during day sampling and four additional species during night sampling.
reportedStudy.lifeStageContextAsReported: The RIS says the majority of fish in the study were juvenile to sub-adult.
notReportedInReviewedSources: Exact sampling dates/months, stations, or coordinates.
Sampling method/gear, effort, individual counts, or abundance estimates.
Voucher specimens, accession numbers, identification authority, or repository.
A direct citation identifying the underlying 2001 ERDB field report or dataset.
Item-specific redistribution or derivative-use permission for the reported list.

lineageAssessment.jicaRelationship: JICA reproduces the same eight names and day/night grouping, then explicitly attributes the paragraph to the 2013 LPPCHEA Ramsar Information Sheet. Treat it as a derivative summary, not independent survey corroboration.
lineageAssessment.bacoorRelationship: The Bacoor committee report states an aggregate of eight fish species but does not name them or cite a source. Its matching count alone is insufficient to establish that it refers to the same ERDB survey or independently validates the list.
lineageAssessment.alba2009Lead: The RIS bibliography includes Alba et al. (2009), Ecological Profiling and Characterization of the Las Piñas-Parañaque Critical Habitat and Ecotourism Area, DENR-NCR Report. The RIS does not explicitly tie the fish paragraph to this reference, so it remains a retrieval lead rather than a proven source lineage.
lineageAssessment.boundedSearchNote: Bounded public searches for the cited 2009 report and the underlying 2001 ERDB fish survey did not locate a directly reviewable primary fish dataset or report. This does not show the material is unavailable or nonexistent.

interpretation.evidenceType: Historical secondary report of ERDB fish sampling, reproduced in an official Ramsar site information sheet; JICA explicitly cites that RIS as its source.
interpretation.geographicResolution: LPPCHEA site context only; no station-level point, shoreline segment, lagoon subdivision, or waterbody geometry is established.
interpretation.taxonomicResolution: Preserve the eight names exactly as printed. The underlying specimens, identification basis, and source-faithful taxonomic status have not been independently verified.
interpretation.temporalMeaning: A report of sampling in 2001; it does not establish present-day occurrence, persistence, population size, or absence.
interpretation.bacoorCountMeaning: A separate aggregate count-only statement with no documented source lineage; do not merge it with the RIS record.

limits: The RIS is a secondary site information document, not the underlying ERDB raw dataset or field report.
JICA's matching passage is explicitly derivative from the RIS and is not an independent survey.
The Bacoor report supplies only an unattributed aggregate count; matching counts do not prove shared provenance.
No record is suitable for asserting current species presence, a catchable stock, diet, legal status, safety, seasonal advice, or exact locality.
No species image, full source text, fish table, or report figure is cleared for app reuse by this review.
No item-specific reuse license or redistribution permission was identified.

decision.reason: Record the official source lineage and the county report's unsupported aggregate separately. Seek the underlying ERDB report or the Alba et al. 2009 ecological profile before considering any site/taxon assertion.

nextActions: Search public library, DENR-NCR, ERDB, and Ramsar reference records for the full Alba et al. 2009 ecological profile; verify whether it cites or reproduces the 2001 ERDB fish work.
Search ERDB research/accomplishment catalogs for the 2001 LPPCHEA fish survey, and request only its bibliographic citation or public repository location if no public copy is indexed.
If a primary report is found, verify survey date, stations, gear, effort, individual counts, vouchers, original taxon labels, and item-specific reuse terms before making a distinct evidence decision.
Keep NCR marine, brackish/wetland, and freshwater source lanes separate; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: Official 2013 Ramsar Information Sheet for LPPCHEA, including the historical 2001 ERDB fish summary and its bibliography.
JICA Appendix 17 reproduces the same eight-fish day/night summary and explicitly names the February 2013 LPPCHEA RIS as its source.
Bacoor City Council committee report with an aggregate eight-fish statement on page 1; no taxa or source citation were found in the six-page PDF.
